lines.say: One tiny bite just turned
this boy's face to pure shock.
Everyone sees a pretty boy startled at the table.
A rose sits in his hair.
His other palm flies up.
And a lizard hangs from his finger.
Caravaggio painted him around 1595.
Critics later said he could
only paint still scenes from life.
So why paint a boy
in the middle of a scream?
The answer may be in his hands.
Michael Fried saw a hidden self-portrait here.
One hand reaches out, one lifts,
like a painter with a palette.
Roberto Longhi traced
the bite to a drawing by Sofonisba Anguissola.
It isn't just a boy.
It may be the painter himself.
So is this a frightened boy,
or a painter bitten by his own lizard?
